rules.frameworks: NHS Supply Chain framework names matching /\b(urology and bowel|endourology|intra-urethral|lithotripsy|bladder scanners|brachytherapy seeds|rigid endoscopy|flexible endoscopes|surgical implants for men)\b/i. NHSSC names a framework after its clinical category, so the name is the key; the CBU category field is far too broad to filter on. COVERAGE LIMITS, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN. Two of the nine agreements above, Rigid Endoscopy and Flexible Endoscopes, are capital routes shared with other specialities, and their suppliers are endoscope manufacturers rather than urology houses; three more, Urology and Bowel Management, Surgical Implants for Men's and Women's Health and Brachytherapy Seeds, are shared with continence, gynaecology and oncology. Being named on a framework is not evidence of volume on this patch, and being absent from one is not evidence of absence from the market. One agreement the page carries is missing here for a data reason rather than a judgement: Maintenance, Repair and Calibration of Medical Equipment, which names urodynamics and lithotripsy equipment among the estates it maintains, is not one of the 121 framework names the Hub's crawler holds, so it cannot be claimed. Five of the nine agreements share one procurement reference, 2021/S 000-007768, and all five end on 31 March 2028 — that reference wraps NHS Supply Chain's whole diagnostic capital portfolio and 22 of its 140 briefs carry it, so its expiry is not a urology event. Finally, the larger half of the catheter economy is bought in the community on prescription through NHSBSA Drug Tariff Part IX and the dispensing appliance contractors, a route with no NHS Supply Chain framework page at all; the Drug Tariff summary is where it appears.

rules.awards: Award-stage notices whose TITLE matches /\b(urolog\w*|endourolog\w*|prostat\w*|transurethral|turp|turbt|holep|cystoscop\w*|ureterosc\w*|nephroscop\w*|resectoscop\w*|urodynam\w*|uroflow\w*|lithotrip\w*|eswl|pcnl|ureter\w*|urethr\w*|nephrostom\w*|nephrolithotom\w*|penile|testicular|orchidectom\w*|orchidopex\w*|vasectomy|varicocele|circumcision|erectile dysfunction|holmium|thulium|green ?light laser|brachytherapy seeds?|urinary catheters?|urostom\w*|bladder scanner\w*|bladder cancer|bladder tumou?r|overactive bladder|neurogenic bladder|bladder washout|bladder irrigation|bladder instillation|urine meters?|urine flow)\b/i and does not match /\b(intravascular)\b/i. The exclusion list exists because every pattern in it matched a real notice that was not this speciality. A CPV code beginning 33125 is recorded as corroboration where the feed carries one, but never admits a notice on its own: a notice carrying a basket of CPV codes is filed under all of them and bought under one. Buyer names are never matched on.
rules.openTenders: Notices still open for bidding, matched the same way. An empty list means no open notice on this patch today, not that none was looked for.
rules.drugTariff: NHSBSA Drug Tariff Part IXA/IXB/IXC for the stated effective month, narrowed to the lines whose virtual medicinal product description matches /\b(nelaton|foley|dilatation catheter|reusable catheter|catheterisation packs?|catheter (?:disposable|retaining|safety|securement|maintenance|valves?)|urinar\w*|urostom\w*|uridome|suprapubic|penile sheaths?|incontinence sheaths?|leg bags?|night bags?|bladder (?:infusion|irrigat\w*|washout)|urine (?:meters?|bags?))\b/i, and then summarised. The part is sliced rather than claimed whole because the part is not this speciality: Part IXA is 56,833 lines of dressings and elastic hosiery, which are the tissue viability page's, and only the lines this pattern selects belong here. Every count and price below is taken from those lines. Prices are the reimbursement price at publication, converted from the pence NHSBSA publishes, and are not necessarily today's.
